gateAccess.githubActionsUrlGoes: GitHub Actions: the URL goes in a secret named INTENTIC_GATE_URL
gateAccess.passFailBlockedOne: of pass, fail or blocked, with one line of why. The token in the URL is the whole auth: keep it in your CI's secret store, never in a committed file.
gateAccess.postWhatPipelineKnows: POST what the pipeline knows, commit, branch, preview URL, and the reply waits for the run: an
gateAccess.sureEveryPipelineWired: Sure? Every pipeline wired to this URL has to be handed the new one.

gatePanel.allowlistCommaSeparatedAnything: An allowlist, comma-separated. Anything else the field says fails the gate: "mostly-pass" does not ship.
gatePanel.gateGivesWorkflowWebhook: A gate gives this workflow a webhook a CI pipeline can call: the pipeline POSTs what it knows, the whole design runs, and the reply is pass, fail or blocked: read off one declared field, never scraped out of prose.
gatePanel.gateReadsDeclaredOutput: A gate reads a declared output field, and no step declares one yet. Give the deciding step a data field first: select it on the canvas and add one under Advanced.
gatePanel.removeGateUrlStops: Remove the gate: its URL stops working, and a future gate gets a new one
gatePanel.savingMintsWebhookUrl: Saving mints the webhook URL: it appears here and under the gate badge on the workflow's tile.
gatePanel.spendCeilingEveryCall: The spend ceiling. Every call runs the whole graph, and a push-triggered pipeline calls on every commit.

loopForm.alreadyLoopName: You already have a loop with that name.

contextNote.continue: Each round continues the same session. Cheaper and it keeps the reasoning, but a long loop starts agreeing with itself.
contextNote.fresh: Every round starts a new session against the same working tree, and carries its notes in a progress file. Slower per round, and it does not drift.

loopForm.everyPublicFunctionDoc: Every public function has a doc comment explaining why it exists.
loopForm.fixesFailuresOneAt: fixes failures one at a time until the suite passes
loopForm.idleRoundOneChanged: An idle round is one that changed nothing in the tree: that, not an error, is how a loop usually goes wrong.
loopForm.name: Name it
loopForm.optionalLeaveEmptyAgent: Optional. Leave it empty and the agent works towards whatever you type in the message box, however it sees fit.
loopForm.optionalOneLineUnder: Optional. One line under the name in the picker.
loopForm.runTestsPickTop: run the tests, pick the top failure, fix it

stopNote.claim: The agent writes a verdict each round. Self-assessed, so it is advisory: pair it with a tight round ceiling.
stopNote.command: Run after every round. Exit 0 ends the loop. The only check here whose answer does not come from a model.
stopNote.judge: A separate model, which did none of the work, rules on the agent's own report against your rubric.

loopForm.whatYoullPickMessage: What you'll pick from the message box. Short enough to read on a button.

stepInspector.acrossEveryRoundStep: Across every round of this step. Empty leaves it uncapped.

hint.goal: Empty, measured against what the run was asked to do. Or set its own bar: "the whole test suite passes".
hint.prompt: Empty, this step does whatever the run was asked to do. Or give it a job of its own: "run the tests, take the top failure, fix it".
hint.rubric: A rubric for a reviewer that did none of this work.
hint.title: Fix the failing tests

stepInspector.leavesWorkNothingElse: It leaves its work and nothing else, so it needs a check below or nothing can tell it it is finished.
stepInspector.name: name
stepInspector.oneSessionFinishedFinishes: One session, finished when it finishes. Ask for an output or a check below to make it repeat until this is true.
stepInspector.pinOneWhereModel: Pin one where the model is part of the design: two steps on two providers is how you compare them. Left alone, this step runs on whatever you normally use.
stepInspector.repeatsUntilTrue: It repeats until this is true.
stepInspector.stepRunsNobodyAt: A step runs with nobody at the keyboard, so it reaches no logged-in account unless it acts as a persona: the persona also sets how far its tools go and where it works.
stepInspector.whatBelongsHereModel: what belongs here: the model reads this
stepInspector.writesDoneHereWhy: It writes "done, and here is why": self-assessed, so pair it with a check below on anything expensive.

templates.boundsEveryResearcherMust: the bounds every researcher must respect: time window, geography, scope, or "none"
templates.calledByPipelineOver: Called by a pipeline over its webhook: a session inspects the change the pipeline named, judges whether it should ship, and answers with a verdict the pipeline can gate the release on.
templates.concreteRequirementsFinalSynthesis: concrete requirements the final synthesis must satisfy, including verification still needed
templates.firstResearchersBriefObjective: the first researcher's brief: objective, key questions, preferred sources
templates.intelligentStepCiPipeline: The intelligent step for a CI pipeline. The pipeline POSTs what it knows, commit, branch, preview URL, to this workflow's own webhook, one session exercises the change and judges it, and the pipeline reads back pass, fail or blocked.
templates.n0To100Score: 0 to 100 score for Attempt A against the request and repository evidence
templates.n0To100Score2: 0 to 100 score for Attempt B against the request and repository evidence
templates.n3To6Words: 3 to 6 words, sentence case, letters and numbers only: names the report and the notes folder
templates.oneRequestBuiltTwice: One request, built twice at once by different models in their own worktrees, then read side by side and merged into the version worth keeping.
templates.oneRequestBuiltTwice2: One request built twice at once, then scored blind by a third model against the repository, and merged under a completion check that reads the score's requirements back.
templates.oneSentenceOnWhy: one sentence on why, the only line of this the pipeline log will show
templates.questionBecomesPlanThree: Your question becomes a plan with three angles; three researchers each take one, in parallel, and write sourced notes; one writer reads all three and delivers a report that answers the question, citations inline.
templates.questionDecomposedIntoThree: A question decomposed into three subtopics, researched in parallel with every claim sourced, and synthesised into one report with inline citations and an honest account of what could not be found.
templates.sameRaceGradedThird: The same race, graded: a third model scores both diffs without knowing who wrote them, and the merge cannot finish until an independent judge accepts its verification.
templates.secondResearchersBriefDisjoint: the second researcher's brief, disjoint from the first
templates.specificDefectsOmissionsRegression: specific defects, omissions, or regression risks, each prefixed with A or B
templates.specificStrengthsWorthPreserving: specific strengths worth preserving, each prefixed with A or B
templates.thirdResearchersBriefDisjoint: the third researcher's brief, disjoint from the other two
templates.whatTypeGoesTo: What you type goes to Claude and to GPT at the same moment, each building it on a branch of its own. A third session then reads both diffs, keeps what each got right, and writes the merged version.

workflowDesigner.couldntSave: The workflow could not be saved.
workflowDesigner.howManyStepsMay: How many steps may run side by side. Every one of them works in a worktree of its own.

workflowRunPage.couldntStop: The run could not be stopped.

workflowsView.copySavingHereReplaces: You have a copy: saving from here replaces it.
workflowsView.couldntRemoveLoop: The loop could not be removed.
workflowsView.couldntRemoveWorkflow: The workflow could not be removed.
workflowsView.couldntSaveLoop: The loop could not be saved.
workflowsView.loopAlreadyRunningKeeps: A loop already running from it keeps going: it copied what it needed when it started.
workflowsView.noLongerOnRecord: is no longer on the record: the ledger keeps the last 50 runs.
workflowsView.runHistoryStaysEvery: Its run history stays: every run kept its own copy of the design. A run already going is not stopped.
